thread:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High error rate and latency for model group 'gptx-8tp' in us-west-2. KV cache memory for tp-shard-group-17 at 92% growth over last 5m; NCCL stalls observed on 3/8 GPUs. Severity: P1. Link: https://metrics.redwood/internal/alerts/1855550123

amy (oncall): saw the pager. taking it. pulling runbook now — could be continuous-batching cache blowup. starting collection of logs + diag.

raj (eng-runtime): noted: we rolled batch-config v3.2 to gptx-8tp ~25m before alert. v3.2 increased continuous_batch_window and allowed unbounded prefix caching w/ tp-shards. suspect shard unevenness + cache growth. quick mitigation: reduce max_batch_tokens and disable continuous batching for this model.

kevin (eng-sre): I'll prepare a rolling shard restart and flush KV cache on affected nodes to get memory back. plan: 1) traffic-steer off tp-shard-group-17 to fallback variant 2) apply hotfix to runtime config 3) restart shard processes. stepping through now.

amy (oncall): runbook step 4 says to check NCCL logs, posting relevant tail:

```
[2028-06-07T14:02:11Z] NCCL WARN: operation timed out (op=allreduce, ring=3), peer 10.0.5.23 unresponsive
[2028-06-07T14:02:12Z] KV_SHARD: excessive pending merges (1243), mem_used=87%
[2028-06-07T14:02:13Z] runtime: continuous_batch consumer backlog spiked to 12k reqs
```

raj (eng-runtime): confirms those logs align w/ uneven partitioning — some shards have much larger key sets due to new prefix caching. quick config patch I want to push: `runtime: { models: { \"gptx-8tp\": { continuous_batching: false, max_batch_tokens: 2048 } } }`

kevin (eng-sre): deploying patch to config service in read-only canary first, then to affected nodes. executing traffic-steer now: `redwoodctl traffic steer --from tp-shard-group-17 --to fallback-small-variant --percent 100 --dry-run=false`

deploy-bot: Starting config deploy 1855550123-hotfix to service runtime-config (canary 10% -> 100%). CI checks: pass.

cs-lead: FYI — we've got a high-touch customer (acme-payments) on the impacted model. They're seeing 5xx's and >5s tail latencies. Please post ETA for mitigation and whether to enable fallback at request-level.

amy (oncall): ETA: immediate mitigations in progress. traffic steering done, will confirm error-rate trend. asking product-ops to notify accounts if customer visible impact persists >30m.

lia (next-oncall): I'm taking handoff — summary: config v3.2 caused aggressive prefix caching; KV cache growth uneven across TP shards caused NCCL stalls and backlog. Actions in-flight: traffic-steer to fallback, config patch to disable continuous batching + lower max_batch_tokens, KV cache flush + rolling shard restart. I'll monitor metrics and coordinate rollback if needed.

raj (eng-runtime): to be safe, also enabling a temporary limiter on prefix insertion: `kv_cache.max_prefixes_per_request=100` to stop new blowups during catchup. Will post PR link in a sec.

kevin (eng-sre): cache flush command executed on nodes [node-17a,node-17b,node-17c]. restarting shard daemons with stagger 30s.

[~8 minutes later]

amy (oncall): seeing latency drop on p50/p95; error rate trending down from 4.2% -> 0.6%. NCCL stalls no longer emitting new errors.

deploy-bot: config deploy 1855550123-hotfix completed to 100% at 2028-06-07T14:23:40Z.

cs-lead: relaying to acct team: we advised acme-payments to route traffic to fallback for next 1h; they confirmed acceptance.

product-ops: logging customer impact window: 2028-06-07T14:01:23Z — 2028-06-07T14:21:00Z. severity P1 for that window.

raj (eng-runtime): follow-ups: 1) automated test for uneven prefix distribution on tp-shards 2) guardrails in deployment pipeline to prevent increasing continuous_batch_window without perf signoff 3) long-term: implement shard rebalancer to avoid hot partitions.

kevin (eng-sre): creating incident postmortem draft and scheduling short blameless sync. tagging infra and runtime teams.

lia (next-oncall): handoff notes posted to #eng-oncall. next steps for oncall: keep an eye on KV cache growth for 24h; revert or roll forward depending on metrics.

amy (oncall): thanks team. paging cleared. will leave channel open for 1h for any lingering regressions. :white_check_mark:
